newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $61, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $61, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Panhandle feedlot cattle were lightly bid at $61.00 per cwt early Tuesday but the bids were passed by owners pricing cattle at $62.00-$63.00 after Monday's active trade at $62.00, feedlot sources said.
"I think the packer was a little surprised at how easy it was to buy cattle at $62.00 yesterday," a Texas source said.
The sales at $62.00 were down $1.00 from last week.

About 50,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area and an estimated 40,000 traded in Kansas amid activity that began light but gained momentum as the day progressed, cattle feeders said.
At $62.00, cattle owners reportedly were losing an average of $50.00 per head, but the losses were grudgingly being accepted so that feedlots could remain current, a Kansas feedlot operator said.
Feedlots were trying to remain as current as possible because of large cattle supplies seen through July, he said.

The hefty supplies were reflected by a steep increase in the Panhandle showlist, which was up 17,000 head from last week. Part of the increase was tied to carryover supplies of cattle not sold during last week's short holiday schedules, feedlot sources said.
